screening_decisions.reason: This is a PET receptor binding study examining 5-HT2A receptor occupancy in patients already on treatment, not a randomized controlled trial comparing treatments. It is an observational pharmacological study rather than an interventional trial.

This is a randomized double-blind multi-center study comparing amisulpride to flupentixol (a typical antipsychotic) in 132 patients with acute schizophrenia. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.

This is a double-blind randomized study comparing amisulpride to fluphenazine (a typical antipsychotic) in 40 hospitalized patients with unproductive schizophrenia. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.
This is a scale development paper describing the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale. It is not a clinical trial and does not involve amisulpride or any treatment comparison.
This is a Cochrane systematic review comparing clozapine to typical antipsychotics. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial and does not involve amisulpride.
This is a review article summarizing amisulpride's properties and efficacy. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.

This is a 4-week double-blind randomized study comparing fixed doses of amisulpride (400, 800, 1200 mg/day) to haloperidol (16 mg/day) in 319 patients with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.
This is a scale development paper for a depression rating scale. It is not a clinical trial and does not involve amisulpride or schizophrenia treatment.

This is a PET study examining dopamine D2 receptor occupancy in 11 schizophrenic patients on chronic amisulpride treatment. It is an observational pharmacological study, not a randomized controlled trial comparing treatments.

This study evaluates neuroendocrine profiles of two new antipsychotic drugs compared to amisulpride. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing amisulpride to placebo or other antipsychotics for treatment efficacy.
This is a retrospective economic assessment using chart data from 160 patients. It is not a randomized controlled trial; patients were randomly selected for chart review, not randomized to treatment.

This is a multi-centre, randomised, parallel-group, double-blind study comparing amisulpride (100 mg/day) to placebo in 141 patients with predominantly negative symptoms of schizophrenia over 6 months. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs placebo, schizophrenia population.

This is a multicenter, double-blind trial comparing 800 mg/day amisulpride to 20 mg/day haloperidol in 191 patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia over 6 weeks. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.

This is a 12-week, multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled trial comparing amisulpride (50 mg/day and 100 mg/day) to placebo in schizophrenic patients with predominantly primary negative symptoms. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs placebo, schizophrenia population.

This is a double-blind trial comparing amisulpride to placebo, but the population consists of non-psychotic subjects with negative syndrome who never presented psychotic symptoms. The selection criteria specifies schizophrenia or other non-affective serious mental illnesses, which this population does not meet.
This is a scale development paper describing the Nurses' Observation Scale for Inpatient Evaluation. It is not a clinical trial and does not involve amisulpride or any treatment comparison.
This is a review article discussing various treatment strategies for schizophrenia, including references to amisulpride studies. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.

This is a one-year randomized study comparing amisulpride to haloperidol in 60 long-term in-patients with schizophrenia and predominant negative symptoms. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.
This is a scale development paper describing the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS). It is not a clinical trial and does not involve amisulpride or any treatment comparison.

This is a double-blind study comparing amisulpride to haloperidol in 41 schizophrenic patients over 42 days. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.
This is a review article summarizing evidence about amisulpride's efficacy and tolerability. It does not report a primary randomised controlled trial.
This study describes development and validation of a rating scale for akathisia. It is not an intervention trial comparing amisulpride to any comparator.

This is a multicentre, double-blind, flexible-dose RCT comparing amisulpride to haloperidol (a typical antipsychotic) in 199 patients with paranoid schizophrenia or schizophreniform disorders. Meets all selection criteria.
This study describes development of assessment scales for chronic psychotic patients. It is not an intervention trial comparing amisulpride to any comparator.
This is a parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT comparing amisulpride (100 mg/d and 300 mg/d) to placebo in 104 in-patients with schizophrenia. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article summarizing published clinical experience with atypical neuroleptics in children and adolescents. It is not a primary RCT.

While this is a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial involving amisulpride in autism (a non-affective serious mental illness), the comparator is bromocriptine (a dopamine agonist), not placebo or an antipsychotic drug. Does not meet the specific comparator criteria.

This is an open (unblinded) trial comparing amisulpride to fluoxetine (an antidepressant) as adjunctive treatments to haloperidol. The comparator is not placebo or an antipsychotic, and the study lacks blinding.
This study is about airway resistance measurement in respiratory medicine. It is completely unrelated to schizophrenia or amisulpride.
This study describes modification and validation of a rating scale for extrapyramidal side effects. It is not an intervention trial comparing amisulpride to any comparator.
This is described as an 'open clinical study' without randomization or control group. The abstract only mentions pharmacological screening results. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
